name: Grazyna Palczewska
title: Project Scientist
affiliation: Brunson Center for Translational Vision Research & Gavin Herbert Eye Institute, USA
details: Grazyna Palczewska, PhD is a Project Scientist at the Department of Ophthalmology in the School of Medicine. Dr. Palczewska is advancing custom-developed non-invasive, high-resolution two-photon ophthalmoscopy imaging for routine quantitative evaluation of certain biochemical processes within the healthy, disease and therapy impacted retina. She developed and continue advancing assays and equipment to visualize and quantify impact of the retinal therapies and drug candidates on retina preservation. This includes small molecule, antibody bound ligands and gene editing. Her publications in PNAS outlined the road to safe and informative two-photon imaging in humans. This research was crowned with 2022 Journal of Clinical Investigation where she was part of the team that presented first data on two-photon imaging of the retina in human subjects. Furthermore, because exchange of ideas and expertise among scientists from around the globe is crucial for the progress and competitive research she coordinates Ophthalmology Research Seminars, now word-wide recognize seminar series.
country: Brunson Center for Translational Vision Research & Gavin Herbert Eye Institute, USA

name: Frans Vinberg
title: Professor
affiliation: Brunson Center for Translational Vision Research, UC Irvine, USA
details: Dr. Vinberg has over 10 years of experience in ocular research, specifically in retinal (patho)physiology. He has developed and commercialized a novel instrument to measure electrical activity of the retinal cells from ex vivo animal or human donor retina samples. He is currently tenured Associate Professor in the department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at the Brunson Center for Translational Vision Research, UC Irvine. His research is focused on understanding the mechanisms in the photoreceptor cells that enable vision over a wide range of light intensities from a cloudy moonless night to a sunny day on the powdery slopes. Furthermore, his goal is to elucidate how these mechanisms are affected in the major blinding diseases including Age-Related Macular Degeneration and Retinitis Pigmentosa. In his free time, you can find Frans skiing, swimming or watching Formula 1 races.
country: Brunson Center for Translational Vision Research, UC Irvine, USA

name: Raunak Sinha
title: Associate Professor
affiliation: Department of Neuroscience, University of Wisconsin–Madison, USA
details: Raunak did his undergraduate studies in human physiology at Presidency College, University of Calcutta. After a year long research at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, Mumbai, he went on to pursue graduate studies in Neuroscience at the International Max Planck Research School, University of Goettingen, Germany. During graduate studies he worked with Jurgen Klingauf in the Dept. of Membrane Biophysics at the Max-Planck Inst. for Biophysical Chemistry headed by Nobel Laureate, Erwin Neher. He studied properties of synaptic transmission in hippocampal neurons – exo-endocyatosis of synaptic vesicles – using single molecule optical microscopy. Thereafter, he moved to Seattle and joined the lab of Fred Rieke for post-doc where he worked on cellular and circuit function in the retina. Here he did foundational work on identifying novel mechanisms by which key neural circuits operate in the fovea – a specialization in the retina (almost) unique to primates that dominate our visual experience. His lab addresses fundamental questions about retinal structure and function in diverse model systems with the aim of understanding cellular, synaptic and circuit mechanisms that shape diverse visual computations.
country: Department of Neuroscience, University of Wisconsin–Madison, USA

name: Valerie Fradot
title: Research Engineer
affiliation: The Institut de la Vision, Paris, France
details: Valérie Fradot embodies an unwavering passion for cell culture and an inspiring career path that demonstrates the importance of perseverance. Currently a research engineer and operational manager of the cell culture platform at the Vision Institute, Valérie is a key figure in the field of ophthalmological research. Her journey began in the 1990s, when Valérie failed her oral exam for her biotechnology baccalaureate and left high school without a diploma. After a year of odd jobs, she found an internship at the CNRS in Strasbourg, where she discovered neuronal cell culture and trained as a research technical assistant. In 1992, her meeting with José-Alain Sahel, the future founder of the Vision Institute, marked a turning point. Joining the

team, Valérie discovered her calling in cell culture. Thanks to José-Alain Sahel's support, she validated her professional experience and obtained a two-year technical degree (BTS) in 1999, followed by an engineering degree while working. Promoted to research engineer in 2013, she became an essential expert, contributing to the development of most of the cell models used at the Institute. Among her major contributions, Valérie developed a protocol for the culture of human and porcine retinas, and adapted screening techniques for cone photoreceptors, an innovation patented in 2023.
country: The Institut de la Vision, Paris, France

name: Blanca Arango-Gonzalez
title: Senior Staff Scientist
affiliation: Institute for Ophthalmic Research, University of Tübingen, Germany
shortDescription: Dr. Blanca Arango-Gonzalez is a senior vision scientist and Project Leader at the Institute for Ophthalmic Research, University of Tübingen, Germany, where she leads research focused on proteostasis and neuroprotection in retinal diseases. She obtained her medical degree from the Universidad Nacional de Colombia and later earned a Doctor of Medicine (Dr. med.) in Neuroophthalmology from the University of Tübingen. With more than two decades of experience in retinal research, her work has concentrated on understanding the molecular mechanisms of inherited retinal degeneration and developing mutation independent therapeutic strategies to preserve photoreceptor function and prevent blindness. Dr. Arango-Gonzalez has played leading roles in numerous national and international research initiatives funded by organizations including the European Union, Foundation Fighting Blindness, Pro Retina, and the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research. Her research has been particularly influential in advancing proteostasis based therapies, including the targeting of valosin containing protein (VCP) and protein quality control pathways as novel treatments for retinal degeneration. She has authored numerous highly cited publications in leading journals and has contributed significantly to the translation of experimental discoveries into potential therapeutic approaches for inherited retinal disorders. Her achievements have been recognized through competitive research grants, international collaborations, and scientific awards, establishing her as a prominent contributor to the field of retinal neurodegeneration and ocular therapeutics.
country: Institute for Ophthalmic Research, University of Tübingen, Germany

name: Alexa Klettner
title: Professor
affiliation: Department of Opthalmology, CAU Kiel University, Germany
shortDescription: As a researcher in the field of biomedical application of marine compounds, Alexa wishes to share her expertise and experience. This gives her the opportunity to support interesting projects, interact with innovative groups, find new collaboration and extend her network. As a professor of Experimental Retinology, Alexa is interested in finding new therapies for ophthalmological diseases and especially to utilize the resources of the ocean, as the compounds found in marine organisms offer vast opportunities for new applications and therapeutics. She is the head of the research lab of the Department of Ophthalmology of the University of Kiel, University Hospital (UKSH). UKSH is the main provider for health care in the region and a big university with 27.000 students. The university has a strong reputation both in medical research and in marine research. The lab in the ophthalmology department focuses on the development of new therapies against age-related macular degeneration. A current project where UKSH is the lead partner is the InterReg5a funded “FucoSan – Health from the Sea” where our consortium investigates the extraction, characterization and application of fucoidan in health and cosmetics.
country: Department of Opthalmology, CAU Kiel University, Germany

name: Petri Ala-Laurila
title: Professor (Neurobiology)
details: I am a “kid” who loves science. I did my PhD in Finland (2000- 2003, Engineering Physics, Helsinki University of Technology) and thereafter moved to the USA, where I did two distinct postdoctoral periods: in Boston (2004-2008, laboratory of Dr. Carter Cornwall) and in Seattle (2008-2012, laboratory of Dr. Fred Rieke). The goal of my lab is to establish a new frontier in the Finnish neuroscience community focusing on signal processing in the mammalian retina.

name: Yuanyuan Chen
title: Assistant Professor
affiliation: UPMC Vision Institute, University of Pittsburgh, USA
details: Dr. Yuanyuan Chen joined the vision research field when she worked with Dr. Krzysztof Palczewski in the Department of Pharmacology at Case Western Reserve University. Dr. Palczewski is a renowned biochemist in vision research who made significant contributions in revealing the molecular structure of the visual pigment rhodopsin, as well as in drug development in blinding disease. She holds two pending patents and has published 18 research and review papers.
country: UPMC Vision Institute, University of Pittsburgh, USA

name: François Paquet-Durand
title: Prof. Dr. rer. nat.
affiliation: Institute for Ophthalmic Research, University of Tübingen, Germany
details: Professor François Paquet-Durand is a leading vision scientist and Group Leader of the Cell Death Mechanisms Group at the Institute for Ophthalmic Research, University of Tübingen, Germany. With a background in biochemistry and neuroscience, he earned his PhD from the University of Hannover and later completed his Habilitation at the University of Tübingen, focusing on the visualization of neurodegenerative processes. His research has significantly advanced the understanding of inherited retinal degeneration, particularly the molecular mechanisms underlying photoreceptor cell death and the role of cyclic GMP signaling in retinitis pigmentosa. As Assistant Professor of Neuronal Pathophysiology and Chief Scientific Officer of Mireca Medicines GmbH, he has successfully translated fundamental discoveries into therapeutic development strategies for retinal diseases. Professor Paquet-Durand has coordinated major European research initiatives, secured substantial national and international funding, and authored numerous influential publications in leading journals including Nature Medicine, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, and Progress in Retinal and Eye Research. He is an active member of international vision research societies and has received several prestigious awards recognizing his contributions to translational ophthalmic research and innovation.
country: Institute for Ophthalmic Research, University of Tübingen, Germany

name: Teemu Turunen
title: Chief Scientific Officer
details: Dr. Teemu Turunen is a biomedical engineer, innovator, and technology leader currently serving as Chief Scientific Officer at [Maculaser](https://www.maculaser.com?utm_source=chatgpt.com), a Finnish medical technology company focused on developing non damaging laser therapies for retinal diseases. He earned both his Master's degree and Doctor of Science (Technology) degree in Bioengineering and Biomedical Engineering from [Aalto University](https://www.aalto.fi?utm_source=chatgpt.com), where his doctoral research focused on retinal physiology, photoreceptor function, electroretinography, and mathematical modeling of visual signaling. Prior to joining Maculaser, he worked at Aalto University in several roles including Project Manager, PhD Researcher, and Innovation Agent, contributing to medical device development, technology commercialization, and innovation management. His work has centered on advancing novel retinal therapies and diagnostic technologies, bridging academic research with clinical translation. Through his leadership at Maculaser, Dr. Turunen has played a key role in the development and validation of innovative laser based treatments for retinal diseases, with research outcomes published in leading scientific journals and aimed at improving the management of retinal disorders and preventing vision loss.

name: Antolin Canto
title: Assistant Professor
affiliation: Department of Biomedical Sciences at the Universidad CEU Cardenal Herrera in Valencia, Spain
details: Dr. Antolín Cantó Catalá is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Biomedical Sciences at the Universidad CEU Cardenal Herrera in Valencia, Spain. He holds multidisciplinary training in Pharmacy, Optometry and Vision Science, Human Nutrition and Dietetics, Orthotics and Prosthetics, Bioinformatics, and Biostatistics, complemented by a PhD in Translational Medicine completed in 2023. His research focuses on retinal degeneration, retinitis pigmentosa, oxidative stress, inflammation, neuroprotection, and molecular mechanisms of photoreceptor cell death. Dr. Cantó Catalá has contributed to numerous scientific publications investigating retinal disease pathogenesis, redox imbalance, autophagy, inflammation, diabetic retinopathy, and potential therapeutic strategies for inherited retinal disorders. His work has explored innovative treatment approaches, including progesterone, sulforaphane, dutasteride, and antioxidant-based interventions in experimental models of retinal degeneration. He is an active participant in international vision research conferences such as ARVO, EVER, Pro Retina, and the International Symposium on Retinal Degenerations, where he has presented findings on novel therapeutic targets and disease mechanisms. Through his interdisciplinary expertise and translational research efforts, Dr. Cantó Catalá contributes to advancing the understanding and treatment of retinal neurodegenerative diseases.
country: Department of Biomedical Sciences at the Universidad CEU Cardenal Herrera in Valencia, Spain
